clue.text: Tree given a short pipe to withdraw liquid

parts.note: taken as written
a tap is a short pipe with a valve for drawing liquid from a cask

explanation.surface: A tree is fitted with a little spout to drain off its sap.
explanation.definitionFit: The atap is the nipa palm of South-East Asia, whose leaves are used for thatching.

clue.text: Jock's aim is to enter contest

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to vie is to contend or compete
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman sets his sights on getting into a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is the crossword's stock Scotsman, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Visie is Scots for a look or a careful aim, as along the sights of a gun.

clue.text: Alloy-clad eatery made by construction worker

indicators.note: something clad is wrapped in a covering, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: solder is a fusible metal alloy for joining metals
a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe

explanation.surface: A metal-sheathed diner is built by a man from the building site.
explanation.walkthrough: A caff is British slang for a cheap cafe; 'clad' asks for the alloy to wrap around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffolder erects the scaffolding on building sites, so is a kind of construction worker.

clue.text: A peak's south of gap with dwarf trees

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so the first parts come after the second

parts.note: a chink is a narrow opening or crack
taken as written
Chambers, through a chain of senses, gives pin as a peak; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A mountain top stands south of a pass, among stunted trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinkapins are dwarf chestnut trees of North America, so they fit as small trees.

clue.text: Sheep, one astray, therefore not as it should be

definitions.text: therefore not as it should be

indicators.note: something gone astray has wandered off and is missing

parts.note: the argali is a large wild sheep of Asia
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One sheep has strayed, and so things are amiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the hard part: the gravedigger in Hamlet says 'argal' as a garbled form of Latin ergo.
explanation.definitionFit: Argal is a comic corruption of ergo, meaning therefore, so it is therefore in a mangled form.

clue.text: Fancy no longer getting cross, showing little sign of fire!

parts.note: flam is an obsolete word for a whim or fancy
a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone who no longer fancies anyone stays calm, showing hardly a flicker of fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A flammule is a small flame, as shown in heraldry or religious art, so a little sign of fire.

clue.text: Defeated king being removed and exposed

indicators.note: something being removed is taken away, so a letter goes

parts.note: routed means defeated heavily
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A beaten monarch is deposed and laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Outed means having had one's secret, such as identity or sexuality, made public.

clue.text: Snide remark about awful brat who is regarded with contempt?

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: someone who is regarded with contempt

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: a dig is a sly cutting remark

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone makes a cutting remark about a dreadful child who is despised.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirtbag is slang for a contemptible, worthless person.

clue.text: Two similar hospital departments beginning to enjoy cordial relationship

parts.note: ENT, the ear, nose and throat department, taken twice

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of enjoy

explanation.surface: Two matching wards at a hospital start to get on well together.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT stands for ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale of 1904.

clue.text: Some Scottish ritual in first month

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: inside the end of Scottish and the start of ritual

explanation.surface: Part of a Scottish rite takes place early in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Tishri is the first month of the Jewish civil year, around September and October.

clue.text: Endless good fortune at home comes to a goddess

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: luck is good fortune
someone at home is in
taken as written

explanation.surface: Luck that never ends arrives at the house of a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'a' does double duty in the surface: it is both part of the wordplay and the article in 'a goddess'; the definition is goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucina was the Roman goddess of childbirth, an aspect of Juno or Diana.

clue.text: Dragonflies chase around bottom of garden area

indicators.note: turned around, the letters of the word are moved about

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of garden
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Dragonflies dart about after something at the end of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschna is a genus of large hawker dragonflies, so the name covers dragonflies collectively.

clue.text: Bond foremost of amorists — was model receiving indication?

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of amorists

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: an artist's model sits, or sat, for a portrait
a sign is an indication

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a model for lovers was given a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like James Bond or a tie; here it is a financial instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignat was paper money issued by revolutionary France, secured on confiscated land, so a kind of bond.

clue.text: Chief has wonderful piece of armour

parts.note: super means excellent or wonderful
the visor is the movable front of a helmet

explanation.surface: The boss owns a splendid part of a knight's suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor oversees others at work, so is the chief or boss of a team.

clue.text: What's said to fasten a feather?

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the sound counts

parts.note: to pin is to fasten, followed by a

explanation.surface: A question about how to attach a feather.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does duty in both halves: it follows pin in the sound and starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinna is a botanical and zoological term for a feather, wing or fin, from Latin.

clue.text: EU meets afresh — commotions evident

indicators.note: doing something afresh means making it anew, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: European Union summits held again show signs of disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: An émeute is a popular rising or riot, from French, so émeutes are commotions.

clue.text: Old money in former kingdom

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: inside the end of former and the start of kingdom

explanation.surface: Antique coinage once circulated in a realm that no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the coin: it belonged to Scotland, itself a former kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The merk was an old Scottish silver coin worth thirteen shillings and fourpence, two-thirds of a pound Scots.

clue.text: Dull blockhead, male eliminated in one-to-one competition

parts.note: mat, or matt, means without shine

indicators.note: eliminated means knocked out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a chump is a fool
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A tedious fool, a man knocked out in a head-to-head contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchup is a contest between two opposing players or teams.

clue.text: Ill-natured person and mad one maybe losing head when meeting policeman?

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland is one mad person
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: A grumpy man and a lunatic, perhaps decapitated, in an encounter with a constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Attercop is a dialect word for a spider, extended to a venomous, ill-natured person.

clue.text: Sort of agent bringing set of books to official proceedings

indicators.note: bringing one thing to another means adding it on after it

parts.note: acta are the recorded official proceedings of a body
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An agent delivers a stack of ledgers to formal hearings.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics an actant is the participant in a clause that performs or undergoes the action, a kind of agent.

clue.text: Rodent takes time to penetrate slope

indicators.note: to penetrate something is to get inside it

parts.note: a cant is a slope or tilt
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rodent spends a while burrowing into a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane rat is a large African rodent that feeds on sugar cane and grasses.

clue.text: Steiner's original movement

indicators.note: something original is new and unconventional, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A tribute to Rudolf Steiner's founding philosophical movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The trenise is a figure, or movement, of the quadrille dance.

clue.text: What was distressing to bring up — not right

indicators.note: not here means without, so a letter is left out

parts.note: to unearth is to dig up or bring to light
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone recalls what was painful to raise, which was wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What was' marks an obsolete word, here from Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneath is an archaic, Spenserian word meaning difficult or uneasy, hence once meaning distressing.

clue.text: Greek character probes acid in geological formation

indicators.note: something that probes pushes its way inside

parts.note: tart means sharp or acid in taste
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek investigates acid in rock layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tar pit is a natural pool of asphalt where oil seeps to the surface, a geological formation.

clue.text: Devious angler? Poetically, he'd ____ fish when reporting!

definitions.note: the gap stands for the answer, a poetic verb meaning enlarge

indicators.note: devious means deviating from the straight path, so the letters are turned about

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A sly fisherman always exaggerates the size of his catch when telling the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in-the-blank sentence: the angler's fish grow in the retelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Largen is a poetic word for enlarge or grow larger, which is what an angler does to a fish in the telling.

clue.text: Sad books, a couple getting put down

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting down a pair of letters moves them from the top to the bottom

parts.note: tomes are large books

explanation.surface: Gloomy volumes, two of them being dismissed by critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesto is an Italian musical direction meaning sad or mournful.

clue.text: No more in game, having got two ducks

parts.note: nap is a card game, short for Napoleon
a duck is a score of nothing, like the letter O, so two make OO

explanation.surface: A player is out of a card game after scoring nothing twice.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoo is First World War slang, from French il n'y en a plus, meaning finished or no more.

clue.text: Sacred literature written in five days

indicators.note: something written in is set down inside, so the letters lie within the following words

parts.note: inside the end of five and the start of days

explanation.surface: Holy scripture composed in under a week.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedas are the oldest Hindu scriptures, the sacred literature of early Sanskrit.

clue.text: Librarian sounding a bit wet?

indicators.note: sounding means as heard, so the sound of the word matters

parts.note: dewy means damp with dew

explanation.surface: A question whether a librarian sounds slightly damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Melvil Dewey was the American librarian who devised the Dewey Decimal classification system.

clue.text: One lovelessly imprisoned by king in place with many layers

indicators.note: something imprisoned is held inside walls

parts.note: Henry, a name of several English kings

indicators.note: love is zero, the letter O, so without love that letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A loveless person is locked up by a monarch in a multi-storey building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' are not strata but hens that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hennery is a poultry farm or hen-house, home to many laying hens.

clue.text: Officers producing plans advanced to the front

indicators.note: taking something to the front moves it from its place to the start

parts.note: ideas are plans or schemes
A is the abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: Officers come up with schemes that are pushed forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The A already in the plans word is the one for advanced, moved to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Aides are officers acting as assistants to senior commanders, as aides-de-camp.

clue.text: Large number in America killed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in US usage, a great many
second meaning: the past tense of slay

explanation.surface: Many in the United States were slain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is American slang for a great quantity and also the past tense of slay.

clue.text: Bird surprisingly slow going round thicket endlessly

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other
surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in another order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a copse is a small thicket of trees

explanation.surface: A bird that is unexpectedly sluggish circles a thicket without end.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split in two so they can go round the shortened thicket.
explanation.definitionFit: The scops owl is a small European owl with ear tufts, so a bird.

clue.text: Language of infatuation with body extremity being heard

parts.note: a pash is a schoolgirl crush

indicators.note: being heard means the sound is what counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a toe is an extremity of the body

explanation.surface: Someone speaks the language of love with a foot on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Pashto is the language of the Pashtun people of Afghanistan and Pakistan.

clue.text: I don't like that casual shirt that's jolly!

parts.note: boo is a cry of disapproval
a tee is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes a cheerful-looking T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective but is a noun: Royal Navy slang for a Royal Marine, as is bootee.
explanation.definitionFit: Both jolly and bootee are naval slang names for a Royal Marine, the sea-going soldier.

clue.text: Job involving number, with work getting creature at sea

indicators.note: involving means including, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a chore is a routine task
ten is a number
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A task with figures, together with labour, produces a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Op is short for opus, the usual crossword sense of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A ctenophore is a comb jelly, a jellyfish-like marine animal that swims with rows of cilia.
